reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about Nb-induced grain-boundary precipitation, dispersion strengthening, and quantitative strength/caloric improvements in a specific alloy system, but the cited evidence (E1 on porous ceramics and E2 on HEA second-phase hardening in a different composite) does not directly support these premises for the proposed material.
premises: Nb addition (1–2 at%) will segregate to grain boundaries and form coherent nanoprecipitates in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy.
Grain-boundary nanoprecipitates will refine the microstructure and act as barriers to crack initiation and propagation.
The coherent Nb-rich precipitates will increase toughness and stiffness via dispersion strengthening without interfering with the matrix phase transformation.
The intervention will raise compressive strength by 50–100% over the 48–218 MPa range observed in prior composites.
The caloric response will be maintained within ±10% of its original value.
